Clashing labels get numeric suffixes. Use it to run one analysis over many separate networks at once, or to build test graphs with several components. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [graphs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A non-empty list of graphs with the same directedness. None is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph whose node and edge counts are the sums over all graphs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the list is empty or the graphs differ in directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Equivalent to chaining `disjoint_union()`. Mirrors NetworkX's `disjoint_union_all`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~disjoint_union`) : Combine two graphs, keeping their nodes apart. [](`~union_all`) : Combine any number of graphs, matching nodes by ID. [](`~count_weakly_connected_components`) : Count the weakly connected components. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Each graph keeps its own nodes, renumbered after the ones before it, and no edges are added between the graphs. So a triangle, a path of four and a star of five give twelve nodes in three components. A label that's already in use gets a suffix, `_2` for its second use and `_3` for its third: ::: {#bdc42761 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec pieces = [ ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(3), ec.Graph().add_path_graph(4), ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5), ] combined = ec.Graph.disjoint_union_all(pieces) combined.count_weakly_connected_components() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#a4e1452d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} combined.get_node_df()["label"].to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1', '2', '3', '1_2', '2_2', '3_2', '4', '1_3', '2_3', '3_3', '4_2', '5'] ``` ::: ::: [Transforming graphs](../user-guide/transforming.qmd#side-by-side) puts two graphs side by side with `disjoint_union()`, and explains how their IDs and labels change.
